text:
ben: quick follow-up after the dedicated-gpu orchestration RFC — we need to pick where the scaling decision logic lives. control-plane scaler (centralized) or daemon/operator on the cluster nodes? thoughts? :thinking_face:

mikaela: my 2c: central control-plane gives us easier global policies (cost vs latency tradeoffs) and easier A/B rollout, but it also becomes a single decision surface that needs a lot more telemetry.

cheng: agree. centralized makes routing + topology-aware decisions simpler. downside: higher RPC volume + more coupling to scheduler state.

nina: operator-side has lower latency to metrics (local GPU stats, device-level telemetry). also simpler fail-open for local tenants when network flap occurs. but harder to enforce global fairness.

shankar: concrete tradeoffs we should call out:
- data recency: operator sees immediate GPU occupancy and queue depth, control-plane sees aggregated metrics with delay.
- correctness: who enforces eviction / preemption? operator can evict quickly, control-plane can coordinate cross-pool moves.
- rollout & safety: control-plane can do canary rollouts per tenant/model; operator rollouts require coordinated agent versions.

ben: for eviction responsibilities, proposal: make eviction a local action but gated by a cross-check API from control-plane. i.e. operator can issue graceful-evict, but only if the control-plane marks that tenant as allowed for preemption. That splits fast action vs global policy.

mikaela: sounds sensible. need clear API surface: something like POST /v1/eviction-intent {tenant, pool, grace_ms, reason, marker} and response {allowed: bool, token}. operator stores token and proceeds.

cheng: will we require token validation to be cryptographically signed? or just TTL + monotonic counter? signed token is nice but adds KMS dependency to operators.

nina: short-term: TTL + audit log. long-term: signed JWT token from control-plane with intent claims. keep it optional initially.

shankar: also need to define metrics for scaling triggers. mixing utilization and queue-length has bitten us before. proposed signal set: [gpu_util_percent, avg_queue_len, p99_latency_ms, inflight_tokens]. Use a scoring function with tunable weights per tenant class.

ben: can we sketch a simple scoring pseudo?

```pseudo
score = w_util * clamp(util_pct / 100, 0, 1)
      + w_queue * sigmoid(queue_len / q_scale)
      + w_tail * smoothstep(p99_ms / tail_scale)

if score > scale_up_threshold -> request scale-up
if score < scale_down_threshold -> request scale-down
```

mikaela: +1 for tunable weights. also need hysteresis windows and cooldowns to avoid oscillation. prefer separating reactive (queue-driven) vs proactive (trend-based) modes.

cheng: config surface idea (pool-level CRD or control-plane JSON):

```yaml
scalingPolicy:
  mode: hybrid # reactive | proactive | hybrid
  headroomPct: 12 # keep ~12% spare capacity for bursty tenants
  weights:
    util: 0.4
    queue: 0.4
    tail: 0.2
  cooldownSeconds: 300
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 50
```

nina: headroomPct must be per-tenant-class. infra tenants vs latency-sensitive product tenants. maybe a small table.
ben: ops question: admission control surface — should we expose an API for callers to declare "latency SLO" so admissions can be conservative for high-SLO tenants? or infer from usage patterns?

shankar: expose SLO is better. customers can set slo: {p95: 200ms}. admissions will allocate headroom accordingly. we must treat absent SLO as best-effort.

mikaela: testing plan: unit test scorer math, integration test with synthetic load (mixed tail + burst), and chaos test where control-plane is unavailable and operators must continue making safe local decisions.

cheng: ops-bot FYI: we have a canary autoscaler image pushed to staging registry: autopilot:v3.2.3-canary

ops-bot: deployed autopilot:v3.2.3-canary to staging (cluster: staging-rt). smoke tests: gpu-util trace, queue stress.

nina: rollout plan idea: start with operator-local decisions using conservative headroom (25%), no automatic preemption (only graceful drain), collect telemetry for 2 weeks, then enable control-plane tokens and tuned scoring, then enable cross-pool preemption for best-effort tenants.

ben: last: long-term refactor note — we should unify scaling signals and admission APIs with the Dedicated Reservation system so that ScaleHint / Reservation CRD are first-class. that'll reduce duplicated logic across operators. but that implies migration tooling.

mikaela: +1. we should spec a migration path in the RFC doc.

ben: ok actionable items: 1) draft eviction-intent API (ben), 2) implement scoring lib proto in go (cheng), 3) add per-tenant SLO field to reservation schema (mikaela), 4) write staging chaos test (nina). I'll open issues and tag owners. thanks all :thumbsup:
